statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band on a contained, twice-retraced overnight range, while Stress stays high on multidecade-high long-end yields, a 12-year low in consumer confidence and a dense quarter-end release schedule.
recommendation: Tail is below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. A narrow danger window is flagged from 12:15 to 15:00 UTC covering ADP, the Core PCE and final GDP block, the US cash open and Chicago PMI. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Contained overnight range holds Tail low into the last Core PCE before the October FOMC
body: NQ futures trade near 30,623 after printing 30,737 and 30,540 overnight, a band of roughly 0.64% in which both extremes were retraced rather than held, and price sits back in the middle of that band. ES is tighter still at 7,734 to 7,756 and VIX at 16.02 is flat near the low of its own range. Nasdaq-100 cash closed Monday at 30,339.33, up 0.21%, mid-range and about 90 points below the session high, so the most recent cash print also ended in a retracement rather than at an extreme. This is the second consecutive contained session with no observed directional efficiency, repeated extension or failed-retracement sequence, which is why Tail stays in the low band. The stress picture is different. The H.15 release for September 28 shows the 2-year at 4.92%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.56%, with the 10-year quoted near 5.26% this morning, around the highest levels since 2007 and 2004 at the long end. The Conference Board consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September against a consensus near 89, the weakest reading since April 2014, and JOLTS openings slipped to 7.079 million from 7.335 million. Soft survey data against multidecade-high yields, September sector dispersion of roughly 10 percentage points and a seventh month of the Iran conflict together justify a high Stress reading that can coexist with low Tail. Oil is the live cross-asset channel: WTI trades near $90.41, up about 1.2%, after dipping below $89, and Brent near $97, having approached $108 on Monday when the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was rejected; the SPR release of up to 40 million barrels and partial Saudi pipeline flows have since pulled prices back, which is itself two-way rather than one-way behaviour. Policy expectations shifted overnight: the New York Fed's Williams said there is no need for urgency after the September hike to 3.75-4.00%, and October-meeting odds were pared from a strong majority to roughly even. The schedule is dense. ADP arrives at 12:15 with consensus near 70,000 after 38,000, and Core PCE, headline PCE, final Q2 GDP and personal income and spending all print at 12:30, with core consensus near 3.3% year over year. This is the last core PCE before the October 27-28 FOMC. The US cash open at 13:30 and Chicago PMI at 13:45 fall immediately behind it, and Micron reports fiscal Q4 after the 20:00 close on the final day of the quarter, with a call from about 20:30. Event importance, survey weakness and positioning are treated as Stress and Confidence inputs; conditional Tail is lifted only into the WATCH band across the release, opening-auction and post-close earnings hours, and would require observed persistent one-way structure to move higher.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the past 24 hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on September 29 has none and stays explicitly unavailable. The window opens in the WATCH band with Tail 20 to 24 and Stress in the mid to high 70s through the September 29 US session, peaking at Tail 24 at 15:00 UTC. From 20:00 UTC Tail crossed back under 20 and the mapped state returned to EA_ON, with Tail easing to 15 to 18 and Stress decaying steadily from 71 to 65 across the overnight session as the range tightened. The last nine slots are flat at Tail 15 to 16 and Stress 65.
outlookSummary: The low Tail band is expected to hold through the remainder of the European morning while NQ stays inside its overnight band. Conditional Tail lifts into the WATCH band for the 12:00 to 14:00 UTC hours covering ADP, the Core PCE and final GDP block, the US cash open and Chicago PMI, then decays through the US afternoon if the release is absorbed with normal retracements. A second conditional lift covers the quarter-end close and Micron's fiscal Q4 report and call from 20:00 to 21:00 UTC. The overnight path returns to a contained two-way baseline on the first day of the new quarter, with confidence declining purely as a function of forecast distance ahead of jobless claims and ISM Manufacturing on October 1 and payrolls on October 2.
